Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 5-day history of dry cough every 20–30 min, greenish rhinorrhoea, subjective fever/chills, myalgias; no dyspnoea, chest pain, sputum, or haemoptysis.  
- Past medical history of T2DM and hypertension increases risk of secondary bacterial infection.  
- Likely diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / viral bronchitis.  
- Differential considerations include COVID-19 infection and post-viral/early acute bacterial sinusitis (consistent with DDx).  
- Red-flag advice given: seek review if temperature ≥ 37.5–38 °C persists, cough worsens, purulent sputum or blood appears, dyspnoea or chest pain develops.  
- Supportive care recommended; antibiotics not indicated at present but may be considered if bacterial infection suspected later.  
- Medication safety: continue Lemsip but avoid other paracetamol-containing products concurrently.  
- Chronic disease advice: maintain routine diabetes and blood pressure follow-up; patient currently lacks home glucose monitoring equipment.  

Management Plan
- Continue supportive measures (fluids, rest, Lemsip ≤ 3 sachets/day, cautious use of nighttime cough syrup only if sleep severely disturbed).  
- Purchase home thermometer and monitor temperature.  
- Safety-netting: re-contact healthcare provider if red-flag symptoms arise as above.  
- Arrange usual GP follow-up for diabetes and hypertension monitoring.
